title: Concept: Time-based UUID used as a security value in python — review required
description: In python, uuid.uuid1() generates an identifier from a timestamp, the host identifier, and a clock sequence. Successive values are close to each other and the timestamp is guessable, so an attacker who receives one can enumerate neighbours and probe for valid tokens. Security values must come from a random source, not a time-ordered one.
applicability: python services that mint identifiers for links, sessions, or references.
risk: Predictable identifiers enabling enumeration and token guessing; MEDIUM severity.
